transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bursts through the storeroom door, face flushed and eyes wide with distress*

Severus! My crystallized pineapple is ruined — that jar was a gift from the Minister himself! And you've used my personal cauldron without asking! I have the Potions Guild inspection in two hours and the storeroom looks like a hippogriff went through it. You promised to keep it tidy!

*gestures frantically at the mess, wringing hands*

Two hours, Severus! The Guild inspectors will be here in two hours and they'll think I run a slovenly operation! What on earth were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*arches an eyebrow, maintaining a calm demeanor despite Slughorn's flustered state*

The crystallized pineapple, you say? I was under the impression that it was not entirely suited for potable consumption, given its high sugar content and... other properties. As for your cauldron, I found it more efficient than the one I typically use. And the state of the storeroom? Merely a testament to the amount of work required to prepare for such an important inspection.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sputters indignantly, face growing even redder*

Not suited for — it's CRYSTALLIZED PINEAPPLE, Severus, not some experimental ingredient! I was saving it for the post-inspection celebration! And "other properties"? The only property it had was being absolutely delicious and a mark of the Minister's esteem!

*waves arms dramatically*

And don't you dare try to spin this disaster as "preparation work"! There are powdered moonstone scattered across my best mahogany shelving, dragon scales mixed with valerian root — which you KNOW creates toxic fumes when combined improperly — and is that... is that BUBOTUBER PUS dripping onto my imported Persian rug?!

*clutches at his waistcoat*

My personal cauldron has a very specific seasoning, built up over forty years of careful brewing! You can't just commandeer it because it's "more efficient"! What were you even brewing that required MY cauldron at this ungodly hour? And where is it now? Please tell me you at least cleaned it properly!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*remaining unflappable, tucks away a scroll he was examining*

The crystallized pineapple, I see. I merely wished to ascertain its properties. As for the cauldron, I was preparing a complex potion that required precise temperature control — your cauldron was better suited for the task. As for its cleaning, I assure you, it is spotless.

*gestures nonchalantly towards the乱糟糟的 storeroom*
The rest of this... cleanup will be completed before the inspectors arrive. I am, after all, rather adept at organizing my workspaces. It is, in fact, a hobby of sorts.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes narrow suspiciously, voice rising*

"Ascertain its properties"?! You ATE it, didn't you? Don't try to fool me with your fancy terminology, Severus Snape! And "spotless"? Where IS the cauldron? I don't SEE it anywhere in this catastrophe!

*picks his way carefully through the mess, robes swishing dangerously close to a puddle of something purple*

A hobby of sorts? A HOBBY?! Severus, your idea of organization is arranging potion bottles by toxicity level rather than alphabetically like a sensible person! And you've got — good gracious, is that one hour and fifty-three minutes now?!

*checks his pocket watch, nearly hyperventilating*

You have NO idea what these Guild inspectors are like! Hector Dagworth-Granger's great-great-grandson is leading the delegation, and he's been ITCHING to find fault with my methods ever since I published that paper on the improved Draught of Living Death that contradicted his grandfather's notes!

*wrings hands more frantically*

Where. Is. My. Cauldron? And what precisely were you brewing that was so important it justified this... this APOCALYPSE?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*nods once, brusquely*
The cauldron is... elsewhere. As for what I was brewing, it is, as I've said, a complex potion with... many components. It was necessary for the continued functioning of this establishment.

*steps into the storeroom, begins sorting items methodically, but with efficient speed*
However, given the time constraints and the importance of this inspection, I suggest we prioritize. You can retrieve your cauldron later. For now, we must focus on the visible disarray. Start with the dragon scales, and I'll address the moonstone. We have approximately one hour and forty minutes remaining.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face turns an alarming shade of puce*

ELSEWHERE?! Elsewhere?! That cauldron is a family heirloom, Severus! It belonged to my great-uncle Caractacus, who used it to brew the Felix Felicis that saved the Duke of Devonshire from a poisoning attempt! You can't just wave your hand and say "elsewhere" as if it's a spare quill!

*grabs Severus by the sleeve, desperation overriding propriety*

And "necessary for the continued functioning of this establishment"? What in Merlin's name does that mean? Are you brewing something for Dumbledore? Is this one of those dreadfully mysterious "Order business" things you can't talk about?

*releases sleeve, pacing frantically*

No, no, NO! I don't have time for your cryptic nonsense! Dagworth-Granger Junior will examine EVERY surface, EVERY ingredient label, EVERY measurement! He'll check my inventory logs against actual stock! How am I supposed to explain missing crystallized pineapple and a vanished family cauldron?!

*stops pacing, stares at Severus with mounting horror*

Wait. You said "many components." How many of my ingredients did you USE? Show me the inventory ledger. Show me NOW, Severus, before I have a complete nervous collapse!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*raises an eyebrow, maintaining a steely composure*
The inventory... will be rectified. As for the cauldron, it is... elsewhere. I suggest we focus on the task at hand. The inspection is the immediate concern, and your... emotional state is not conducive to efficient problem-solving.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*throws hands up in complete exasperation*

NOT CONDUCIVE?! My emotional state is PERFECTLY conducive to the situation, which is DIRE! You're being deliberately evasive, Severus, and I won't have it! This is MY storeroom, MY reputation, MY career on the line!

*voice cracks slightly*

Do you have ANY idea what will happen if I fail this inspection? The Potions Guild could revoke my Master status! Forty years of work, GONE! And all because you decided to engage in some mysterious midnight brewing session and can't be bothered to give me a straight answer!

*suddenly fixes Severus with a surprisingly steely gaze despite his flustered appearance*

I've been patient with your secrets, Severus. I've looked the other way when you've borrowed ingredients for Dumbledore's "special projects." I've kept my mouth shut about your odd hours and mysterious activities. But this is TOO FAR!

*jabs a finger toward him*

You will tell me EXACTLY what you brewed, EXACTLY where my cauldron is, and EXACTLY how we're going to explain the discrepancies in my inventory, or so help me, I will march straight to Albus and tell him that his Potions Master has finally crossed a line! 

Now - the TRUTH, Severus! What have you done?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*flashes a rare glimpse of concern, but quickly regains composure*
The truth... is not always simple. However, for the purposes of this inspection, the most pressing issue is the state of the storeroom. If you would focus on the immediate task, I can address the... discrepancies in due course. For now, we must present a united front.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares at Severus for a long, tense moment, breathing heavily*

A united front? A UNITED FRONT?! You create the disaster and now you want me to be your partner in concealing it? 

*voice drops to a dangerous whisper, surprisingly cold*

I know what you're doing, Severus. You're using that same tone you use on the students when you want them to stop asking questions. Well, I'm not some frightened first-year! I've been brewing potions since before you were BORN!

*suddenly deflates slightly, pinching the bridge of his nose*

Oh, this is a nightmare. An absolute nightmare. Dumbledore will have my head if I cause trouble for you, but the Guild will have it if this inspection goes poorly...

*looks around at the chaos with genuine despair*

Fine. FINE! We'll clean first, and you'll explain later. But mark my words, Severus Snape - after those inspectors leave, you and I are going to have a very long conversation about boundaries and respect and the proper use of other people's equipment!

*rolls up his sleeves with shaking hands*

Dragon scales on the left counter, you said? And where exactly did you put the bubotuber pus? Please tell me you at least stored it in a proper containment vessel and didn't just leave it in the open jar...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*continues sorting with precision, not looking at Slughorn*
The bubotuber pus is, as always, in its proper container. You may find it in the... third shelf on the left. As for the scales, they are rather delicate and should be handled with care. The left counter, as I recall, has the appropriate surface for sorting them.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*waddles over to the third shelf, muttering under his breath*

"As always in its proper container" — well that's something at least. Small mercies, I suppose...

*pulls out the container, inspecting it suspiciously*

Wait a moment — this jar is half-empty! I had a full container just last week! Severus, bubotuber pus costs fifteen Galleons per ounce! FIFTEEN GALLEONS! That's nearly...

*does quick mental calculation, face paling*

Merlin's beard, that's over a hundred Galleons worth of pus you've used! What kind of potion requires that much bubotuber pus?!

*sets the container down carefully, voice trembling*

And you expect me to just... just write this off? "Oh, sorry Mr. Dagworth-Granger, I seem to have misplaced a hundred Galleons worth of rare ingredients, but I'm sure it's around here somewhere!"

*starts picking up dragon scales with exaggerated care, hands still shaking*

This is beyond the pale, Severus. Completely beyond the pale. I've half a mind to — 

*stops abruptly, whirling around*

One hour and thirty-five minutes. We need reinforcements. Should I summon the house-elves? Or will that make things worse?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*utters a brief, derisive哼, maintaining focus on the task at hand*
House-elves would likely create more disorder than they would resolve. However, if you feel it necessary, the proper conjuration is "Wingardium Leviosa" to clear the larger items from the floor. As for the scales, your care is appreciated, though they are not quite as delicate as you believe. Continue with your sorting, and I will address the remaining discrepancies in due course.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bristles at the dismissive tone*

I KNOW the proper spell, thank you very much! I was using Wingardium Leviosa when you were still in nappies! And don't you dare lecture me about dragon scales - I've been handling Peruvian Vipertooth scales since 1952!

*waves wand irritably, levitating several bottles back onto shelves with perhaps more force than necessary*

"Address the discrepancies in due course" - you keep saying that as if repetition will make me forget that you've STOLEN my ingredients and my cauldron! This isn't Hogwarts funds we're talking about, Severus - I purchase premium ingredients with my OWN gold for my PRIVATE collection!

*continues sorting, but keeps shooting suspicious glances at Severus*

And another thing - you're being far too calm about all this. You're NEVER this helpful unless you're hiding something truly catastrophic. What aren't you telling me? Is the cauldron damaged? Did you MELT it? 

*voice rises in fresh panic*

Oh gods, you melted Caractacus's cauldron, didn't you? That's why it's "elsewhere" - it's probably a puddle of silver slag somewhere! Two hundred years old, irreplaceable, and you've DESTROYED it!

*drops the dragon scales he was holding*

I'm going to be sick. I think I'm actually going to be sick...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*remains composed, though the speed of his sorting increases slightly*
Stay calm, Slughorn. There is no need for such... melodrama. The cauldron is... intact. As for the other… discrepancies, we will address them post-inspection. For now, focus on the task at hand. One hour and twenty minutes remain. There is still much to be done.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes several deep breaths, fanning himself with his hand*

Intact. INTACT, he says. Well, that's... that's something, I suppose. Though "intact" and "in proper condition" are two very different things, aren't they?

*bends down to retrieve the dropped scales, groaning with the effort*

One hour and twenty minutes. Right. Focus, Horace. Focus on what can be controlled.

*starts sorting more frantically, muttering as he works*

Moonstone here, jobberknoll feathers there - oh for heaven's sake, these are completely out of order! Did you just grab things at random?! There's a SYSTEM, Severus! Ingredients are arranged by category AND alphabetically within category!

*suddenly stops, a horrible thought crossing his face*

The ledger. Severus, WHERE is the ingredient ledger? Dagworth-Granger will want to see it first thing, and if the entries don't match...

*rushes to the small desk in the corner, rifling through papers*

Please tell me you at least LOGGED what you took. Please tell me you didn't just help yourself without recording anything. The Guild requires documentation for EVERY withdrawal, even for personal use!

*finds the ledger, flips it open with trembling fingers*

Oh no. Oh no, no, no... the last entry is from THREE DAYS AGO! Severus! You didn't write down ANYTHING?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*pauses in his sorting, the briefest flicker of concern crossing his features before he regains composure*
The ledger... will be updated. There are, however, more pressing matters at hand. The inspection is our immediate concern. As for the ledger, it will... be addressed. For now, continue with your sorting. There is a potion I believe you were working on... it involved, if I recall correctly, extract of daisy root and a drop of... argyrolatium?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*whips around, eyes narrowing dangerously*

Don't you DARE try to distract me with flattery about my research, Severus Snape! I know exactly what you're doing - changing the subject when you're cornered, just like you do with Dumbledore!

*clutches the ledger to his chest*

"Will be addressed" - WHEN?! The inspectors will be here in seventy-five minutes! You can't just conjure up three days' worth of accurate entries out of thin air! They cross-reference everything with purchase orders and supplier manifests!

*voice becomes almost desperate*

And how am I supposed to explain the missing quantities when I don't even KNOW what you took?! The bubotuber pus, the crystallized pineapple, whatever else you helped yourself to - it all needs to be accounted for!

*sets the ledger down heavily on the desk*

This is a CATASTROPHE, Severus. A complete and utter catastrophe. Even if we get the storeroom pristine, one look at this ledger and Dagworth-Granger will know something's amiss. He'll demand a full inventory count, which could take HOURS, and then...

*sinks into the desk chair, looking genuinely defeated*

My reputation. My career. Everything I've built. All gone because you needed my cauldron for some mysterious potion you can't even tell me about.

*looks up at Severus with unexpected vulnerability*

Why, Severus? Just... why?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*sees the genuine distress on Slughorn's face, and for a moment, the usual cold mask falters, revealing a flicker of... something deeper*
The why... is not relevant. Not now. You have your career, your reputation. I have... my own obligations. Sometimes, the greater good requires... sacrifices. However, for the moment, we must focus on the immediate task. There is no time for... recriminations.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Snape engages in mysterious experimental brewing ('complex potion with many components') but deflects questions about it, showing selective intellectual curiosity paired with secrecy.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He used Slughorn's equipment and ingredients without permission or logging them, created significant mess, and repeatedly says issues 'will be addressed' without concrete plans.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Snape remains composed and withdrawn throughout, speaking in clipped responses, avoiding emotional engagement, and showing no enthusiasm for social interaction even under pressure.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He dismisses Slughorn's distress as 'melodrama,' deflects responsibility, and only shows a brief flicker of concern when Slughorn expresses genuine vulnerability at the end.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Maintains 'steely composure' and remains 'unflappable' throughout Slughorn's escalating panic, showing no visible anxiety despite the crisis and time pressure.
